'''Michael David Resnik''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|r|ɛ|z|n|ɪ|k}}; born March 20, 1938) is a leading contemporary American [[philosophy of mathematics|philosopher of mathematics]].<ref>M. D. Resnik (1974) On the Philosophical Significance of Consistency Proofs, ''Journal of Philosophical Logic'' pp. 133–147 
 [https://www.jstor.org/stable/30226087 URL] [https://dx.doi.org/10.1007%2FBF00652074 DOI]</ref><ref>M. D. Resnik (1981) Mathematics as a Science of Patterns: Ontology and Reference, ''Noûs'' Vol. 15, No. 4, Special Issue on Philosophy of Mathematics, pp. 529–550.  
[https://www.jstor.org/stable/2214851 URL] [https://dx.doi.org/10.2307%2F2215419 DOI]</ref>

==Biography==
Resnik obtained his B.A. in mathematics and philosophy at [[Yale University]] in 1960, and his PhD in Philosophy at [[Harvard University]] in 1964. He wrote his thesis on [[Frege]].<ref>M. D. Resnik (1964) Dissertation: Frege's Methodology: A Critical Study, Harvard University, 274 pp.</ref><ref>M. D. Resnik (1981) Frege and Analytic Philosophy: Facts and Speculations ''Midwest Studies In Philosophy'' Vol. 6, pp. 83–104. [https://dx.doi.org/10.1111%2Fj.1475-4975.1981.tb00430.x DOI]</ref> He was appointed Associate Professor at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 1967, Professor in 1975, and University Distinguished Professor in 1988.<ref>
{{cite web
|url=http://www.unc.edu/gradrecord/2002-2004/faculty.html
|title=UNC Graduate Record 2002–2004}}</ref> He is Professor [[Emeritus]] of [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] and currently resides in rural [[Chatham County, North Carolina]].
